newsitem.title: USA: Plains feedlot cattle sales active at $70-feedlots.
newsitem.headline: Plains feedlot cattle sales active at $70-feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains cattle markets traded in heavy volume at $70.00 per cwt, up $1 from last week's sales, feedlot sources said.
About 25,000 head had sold at Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma feedlots and near 30,000 in Kansas by late Friday morning, sources said.
However, trading was so fast and furious that counts had fallen behind, they said.
"This is going to be a big volume day," one Kansas cattle feeder said.
Feedlot sources said the market had been anticipating $70.00 trades all week amid ideas that packers were getting short on cattle inventories and would need to buy more for next week's operations.
Some packers were so short on supplies they were asking for Monday delivery of cattle bought this morning, cattle feeders said.
Prices were buoyed by tight supplies of market-ready cattle and gains this week in boxed beef prices, which were drumming up packer interest for cattle to fill new beef orders, sources said.
